巴爾巴特琴為撥奏弦鳴樂器，傳統描述為整木鑿製並具木製共鳴板；現代伊朗型琴身較烏德: The barbat is a plucked chordophone, traditionally described as carved from one piece of wood with a wooden soundboard; the modern Iranian type has a smaller body than the oud, a longer neck and a slightly higher fingerboard, and its timbre differs from the oud's. The right hand plucks with a long, soft plectrum (risha or mizrab) at a particular wrist angle, which gives different timbres; a thin pointed plastic plectrum sounds lighter and finer, a thick round one is louder, and trimming the tip can increase the attack volume. Fingernail on the left hand gives a clearer timbre than the fleshy fingertip, and the ornaments are more marked. The source gives no range.

巴爾巴特琴的起源與大伊朗、中亞有關，最早圖像可追溯至公元前1世紀的北巴克特里亞。: The origins of the barbat are connected with Greater Iran and Central Asia, and the earliest image goes back to northern Bactria in the first century BCE. Gandharan sculpture of the second to fourth centuries also shows a similar short-necked lute. In the Sasanian empire its Pahlavi name meant short-necked lute, and it passed from Central Asia into West Asia. Some Arabs were already using it in the sixth century; at the end of the sixth century Nadr made a wooden-topped Persian-style 'ud', which came from Iraq to Mecca. In the seventh century Mansur Zalzal modified it, and the barbat and the 'ud shabut were used together until the tenth century.

The barbat is a short-necked lute from Greater Iran or Persia, popular in Central Asia, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321-6. The traditional form is carved from a single piece of wood, neck included, with a wooden soundboard; historically it may have sounded with a skin face, and it is regarded as the ancestor of the wooden-faced oud, the pipa and the Yemeni skin-faced qanbus. It was played by Persians and some Arabs; modern Iranian luthiers have rebuilt it on that model, with a smaller body, a longer neck and a slightly raised fingerboard. Players mostly sit, supporting it on the thigh and the right arm with the face vertical, and pluck with a quill or plastic plectrum.
持琴時琴面垂直、演奏者看不見，以右大腿與右臂支撐，讓左手在指板上移動。發聲使用長: The instrument is held with its face vertical, where the player cannot see it, resting on the right thigh and right arm so that the left hand can move on the fingerboard. It sounds with a long, soft plectrum touched to the string at a special angle, which gives different timbres. A beginner should stay relaxed and use only the muscles and force needed; the left hand can stop the string with four fingers, or use the nail as well, which makes the timbre clearer and the ornaments more marked.
